surface_enumerated.i18n: 1 module + en.json/ar.json (798 keys each, flat dotted, 100% key parity) + .copy-policy.json
surface_enumerated.typecheck_status: npx tsc --noEmit NOT RUN — SmartCompareApp/node_modules absent in the pinned tree and install is forbidden. Static substitute used: tsconfig strict:true (extends expo/tsconfig.base); 41 `as any`, 83 `: any`, 0 @ts-ignore in non-test src.

findings.title: Camera compare is a dead end on a fresh install — nothing ever requests camera permission on the ScanCamera route
findings.claim: ScanCameraScreen destructures only `permission` from `useCameraPermissions()` and its denied branch renders a title with a close button, so a user routed there before granting camera access can never trigger the OS dialog and the whole scan mode is unreachable.
findings.evidence: ScanCameraScreen.tsx:81 `const [permission] = useCameraPermissions();` — the hook's second tuple element (`requestPermission`) is discarded, and `expo-camera`'s hook defaults to get-only (it never requests). ScanCameraScreen.tsx:226-248 renders `testID="scan-camera-permission"` with only `t('home.permission.title')` ("Snap to compare") plus the close X — no CTA, no `requestPermission()` call, and it deliberately omits `home.permission.body` / `home.permission.cta` / `home.permission.gallery_link`, all three of which exist in en.json:594-596 and ar.json:591-593 for exactly this pad. Contrast HomeScreen.tsx:100 `const [permission, requestPermission] = useCameraPermissions();` and HomeScreen.tsx:510 which wires a real CTA. The route is reachable while denied: HomeScreen.tsx:788 renders the "Open camera" CTA on `canCompare && inputMode === 'scan'` with NO permission condition, and its handler HomeScreen.tsx:483-485 `handleScanCtaPress = () => navigation.navigate('ScanCamera')` navigates unconditionally.
findings.failure_scenario: Fresh install, user taps the Scan mode chip on Home. renderCenterArea shows the permission card (correct), but the bottom 'Open camera' CTA is still rendered and still enabled. User taps it (the CTA is the visually dominant action), lands on ScanCameraScreen, sees 'Snap to compare' + an X, no OS dialog appears and no button exists. The camera comparison feature — one of three compare modes — is unreachable, and the user has no signal that a permission is the blocker.
findings.fix_sketch: Destructure `requestPermission` in ScanCameraScreen and render the full pad (`home.permission.body` + a CTA calling `requestPermission()` + the gallery link), mirroring HomeScreen.tsx:504-521; and gate HomeScreen.tsx:788 / :483 on `cameraPermissionGranted` so the CTA cannot route into the denied state.

findings.title: HomeScreen gallery fallback silently discards the images the user just picked
findings.claim: `pickFromGalleryFallback` launches the image library, then navigates to ScanCamera without passing `result.assets` anywhere, so the selected photos are dropped and the user arrives at the same permission dead end.
findings.evidence: HomeScreen.tsx:461-472 — `const result = await ImagePicker.launchImageLibraryAsync({...selectionLimit: MAX_IMAGES...}); if (!result.canceled && result.assets && result.assets.length >= MAX_IMAGES) { navigation.navigate('ScanCamera'); }`. `result.assets` is read only for the length check. `ScanCamera` takes no params (types/types.ts:562 `ScanCamera: undefined;`) and ScanCameraScreen's slot state is seeded from a module-private `let _slotsCache: Slots = [null, null]` (ScanCameraScreen.tsx:65, read at :83) that only ScanCameraScreen itself writes (:139, :218, :70). HomeScreen never imports or touches it. This handler is the sole `home.permission.gallery_link` action (HomeScreen.tsx:516-521) — the designed escape hatch for users without camera access.
findings.failure_scenario: User denies camera, taps 'Or pick from gallery', selects 2 product photos. Both photos are thrown away and the app pushes ScanCameraScreen, which (per frontend-01) renders the permission dead end. If the user picks only 1 photo the `>= MAX_IMAGES` guard fails and absolutely nothing happens — no navigation, no toast, no error. The no-camera path produces zero comparisons in every branch.
findings.fix_sketch: Either pass the picked URIs through (`navigation.navigate('Results', { vision_products: result.assets.map(a => a.uri) })`, matching ScanCameraScreen.tsx:214-221's own compare hand-off) or export a slot-seeding setter from ScanCameraScreen; and give the <2-selected branch user-visible feedback.

findings.title: Referral bonus comparisons can never be spent — the client compare gate ignores bonus credits and the `tier` field
findings.claim: `canCompare` is `status.used.lifetime < 3` and ignores both the fetched `tier` and the referral `bonusRemaining`, so every compare entry point blocks client-side once 3 lifetime comparisons are used even when the backend would allow the request.
findings.evidence: useComparisonCounter.ts:6 `const FREE_LIMIT = 3;` and :46 `const canCompare = used < FREE_LIMIT;` where `used` is hydrated from `status.used.lifetime` (:22-25). The `UsageStatus` shape it fetches carries `tier: 'free' | 'premium'` and `limits.lifetime_free` (usageService.ts:9,15-19) — both are dropped. HomeScreen separately fetches referral bonus credits into `bonusInfo.bonusRemaining` (HomeScreen.tsx:129-153, from `getReferralStatus().monthly_bonus_comparisons`) but never feeds them into the gate. All four compare entry points short-circuit before any network call: HomeScreen.tsx:275-278 (text), :392-395 (url), :452-457 (mode change), :492-500 (scan area → PaywallBanner). The header pill that would display `+{bonusInfo.bonusRemaining}` is itself wrapped in `{canCompare && (` at HomeScreen.tsx:645, so the bonus becomes invisible at exactly the moment it would matter.
findings.failure_scenario: User consumes 3 lifetime comparisons, invites a friend, the friend signs up, and the backend grants bonus comparisons (referral Loop 1/Loop 2, `ENABLE_REFERRAL_SYSTEM`). On the next launch `used=3` so `canCompare=false`: Home hides the hero, the category strip, the input shell and the header counter, and every compare tap navigates to a Paywall whose CTA is `Alert.alert('Coming soon')` (PaywallScreen.tsx:228-239). The bonus the referral system exists to deliver is both unspendable and unshowable — the entire referral incentive loop terminates in a dead paywall.
findings.fix_sketch: Thread the bonus and tier into the gate: `canCompare = tier === 'premium' || used < (limits.lifetime_free ?? 3) + bonusRemaining`, sourcing `limits`/`tier` from the already-fetched `UsageStatus` instead of the hardcoded 3, and move the header-pill render out from under the `canCompare` guard.

findings.title: 65 t() keys referenced by screens are absent from both en.json and ar.json — Login, Paywall, Profile section headers, History hero and camera preview render English to Arabic users
findings.claim: Sixty-five distinct translation keys used in src/ do not exist in the 798-key catalog, so i18next falls through to each call site's English `defaultValue` in the Arabic locale as well as English.
findings.evidence: Enumerated by matching every `t('<literal>')` in non-test src/ + App.tsx against the keys of src/i18n/en.json: 460 keys referenced, 65 missing. Concentrations: `auth.*` 13 keys (whole Login screen — e.g. LoginScreen.tsx:323 `t('auth.welcomeBack', { defaultValue: 'Welcome back.' })`, :326, :354, :363, :377, :442 and the 6 error strings at :206-278); `paywall.*` 19 keys (PaywallScreen.tsx:265-388, incl. title, subtitle, both plan cards, cta, trust line, terms/privacy and the entire trial timeline); `home.scan.preview.*` 6 (HomeScreen.tsx:532-583); `home.camera.*` 4 (ScanCameraScreen.tsx:277-346); `profile.section.*` 4 (ProfileScreen.tsx:429-581); `history.hero.*` 4 (HistoryScreen.tsx:128-202); `results.empty.*` 3 (ResultsScreen.tsx:669-680); `referrals.bonus.expiresIn*` 3 (BonusCountdownCard.tsx:120-133). The catalog is otherwise at perfect parity (798 EN keys == 798 AR keys, zero one-sided), and __tests__/i18n.test.ts:7 only asserts `enKeys == arKeys` — it never checks that a key a screen calls actually exists, so this gap is invisible to the whole test estate.
findings.failure_scenario: An Arabic user opens the app: the sign-in screen reads 'Welcome back.' / 'Your advisor and credits are waiting.' / 'or' / 'New here?' in English; the Paywall is entirely English including 'HOW THE TRIAL WORKS' and both plan cards; Profile's four section headers are English inside an otherwise-Arabic RTL settings list. Roughly a third of the app's rendered copy escapes localisation with no test or lint signal.
findings.fix_sketch: Add the 65 keys to en.json + ar.json (the English text already exists verbatim in each `defaultValue`), then add a jest fence that walks src/ for `t('<literal>')` and asserts membership in en.json — the same shape as __tests__/i18n/no-deleted-keys.test.ts.

findings.title: The frontend has no blocking CI gate at all — 235 jest files and the eslint i18n fence are never executed, and tsc is continue-on-error
findings.claim: ci.yml defines four jobs and none of them runs the frontend test suite or eslint; the one job that does typecheck is marked `continue-on-error`, so no frontend regression can fail a build.
findings.evidence: ci.yml jobs are exactly `backend-tests` (:10), `backend-lint` (:104), `dependency-audit` (:154), `frontend-typecheck` (:189). `frontend-typecheck` ends at :204-205 `run: cd SmartCompareApp && npx tsc --noEmit` / `continue-on-error: true  # 7 pre-existing TS errors`. `npm audit` at :185-187 is likewise `continue-on-error: true`. There is no `jest` / `npm test` step anywhere in ci.yml or live-suite.yml (grep for jest/npm test returns only comments), and package.json declares no `test` script at all — only `lint`, which nothing invokes. .githooks/pre-commit (the other gate) is Python/SQL only: py_compile, ruff, black, a credential grep and sqlfluff — zero JS/TS steps. Consequences that are already realised in this tree: the eslint `i18next/no-literal-string` fence configured at eslint.config.js:52-63 as `'error'` over src/screens + src/components has un-caught violations (LoadingScreenVariants.tsx:408, PaywallScreen.tsx:331/339/347), and src/i18n/.copy-policy.json's own `_doc` asserts "The jest fence at __tests__/copy-policy.test.ts ... runs on every CI build" — that claim is false.
findings.failure_scenario: A PR deletes an i18n key, breaks the SSE parser, or introduces a TS error: CI is green. The 235 frontend test files (~5,500 assertions across screens, services, primitives and copy policy) exist purely as a local convenience. The measurable cost is that every frontend finding in this report could have been caught by tooling already present in the repo but never wired to a gate.
findings.fix_sketch: Add `test` + `typecheck` scripts to package.json; add a `frontend-tests` job running `npm ci && npx jest --ci` and `npx eslint 'src/**/*.{ts,tsx}'`; drive the 7 tsc errors to zero and drop `continue-on-error` from frontend-typecheck.

findings.title: Google ID-token prefix is console.logged in release builds — CLAUDE.md's "all console.log wrapped in __DEV__" invariant is false and no console-strip transform exists
findings.claim: `console.log('[GOOGLE-DIAG]', diagHead)` runs unguarded on every Google sign-in and prints the first 24 characters of the OAuth id_token to the device log in production builds.
findings.evidence: authService.ts:478-481 — `const parts = idToken.split('.'); const diagHead = \`len=${idToken.length} parts=${parts.length} head=${idToken.substring(0, 24)}\`; console.log('[GOOGLE-DIAG]', diagHead);` with no `__DEV__` guard (it is the only unguarded console call in non-test src/ — the two other grep hits, authService.ts:599 and NewOnboardingHost.tsx:72, sit inside `if (__DEV__)` blocks). babel.config.js contains only `presets: ['babel-preset-expo'], plugins: ['react-native-reanimated/plugin']` — no `transform-remove-console`, so the statement survives into the release bundle and RN evaluates it. CLAUDE.md's Frontend Services section states of authService.ts: "All `console.log` wrapped in `__DEV__`" — a wrong status claim. The same `diagHead` is also fed to `Sentry.addBreadcrumb` (:481) and, on the reject path, embedded in a user-facing error string returned to the caller (:530 `error: \`${rejMsg}. token ${diagHead}. Send this whole message.\``). The block is self-labelled temporary ("Diagnostic Sentry captures remain in place until a clean B4 ships green", :463) and B4 is recorded as resolved at :483.
findings.failure_scenario: Any Google sign-in on a shipped build writes token material to logcat / the iOS unified log, readable by any process with log access on Android <10 and by anyone with the device attached; and a backend rejection puts the same token head into an on-screen error message the user is instructed to screenshot and forward.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the resolved B4-DIAG block (:466-481, :526-531, :536-542) or at minimum wrap :480 in `if (__DEV__)`, drop `diagHead` from the user-facing strings, and add `transform-remove-console` to babel.config.js for production so this class cannot recur.

findings.title: The Sentry scrubber covers exceptions and breadcrumbs but not `event.message` or `event.extra` — the only capture path the app actually uses
findings.claim: `scrubBeforeSend` walks `event.exception.values`, `event.breadcrumbs.values` and `event.request.headers` only, so `Sentry.captureMessage(msg, { extra })` — every explicit capture in the codebase — leaves both the message and the extras unredacted.
findings.evidence: sentry.ts:98-131 handles exactly three branches: `event.exception.values[].value` (:101-107), `event.breadcrumbs.values[].message|data` (:110-119), `event.request.headers` (:122-128). `event.message`, `event.extra`, `event.contexts` and `event.tags` are never touched. The four explicit Sentry calls in non-test src/ are all `captureMessage` with `extra`: authService.ts:471 (`extra: { sdkResultKeys, signInResultShape }`), :481 (breadcrumb — covered), :527 (`extra: { status, code, server_error, diagHead }` where `diagHead` carries the id_token prefix), :538 (`extra: { errCode, errMessage, errDomain, errStack }`). The module docstring (sentry.ts:4-7) claims it "Mirrors the backend scrubbing patterns ... so JWTs, OpenAI / Firecrawl API keys, generic long-hex tokens, and Bearer headers are redacted before events leave the device"; for the app's own capture calls it does not. Note also that a 24-char JWT prefix would not match the three-segment `eyJ...\.eyJ...\..*` pattern at sentry.ts:31 even if `extra` were scrubbed.
findings.failure_scenario: A Google sign-in rejection ships `extra.diagHead` (token prefix) and `extra.server_error` (verbatim backend text) plus `extra.errStack` to Sentry with no redaction, and every future `captureMessage`/`setContext` call inherits the same blind spot.
findings.fix_sketch: Extend `scrubBeforeSend` with `if (typeof event.message === 'string') event.message = scrubString(event.message)` and `if (event.extra) event.extra = scrubDict(event.extra)` (plus `contexts`), and add the corresponding cases to src/services/__tests__/sentry.test.ts.

findings.title: identifyFromImages uses raw fetch, bypassing the 401 refresh interceptor, so an expired session surfaces as a photo-quality error
findings.claim: The camera identify call reads the token by hand and posts with `fetch`, so it never reaches the axios response interceptor that refreshes on 401; ResultsScreen then classifies the failure as `vision_failed`.
findings.evidence: api.ts:159-174 — `const { getToken } = require('./authService'); const token = await getToken(); ... const response = await fetch(...)` with a hand-built `Authorization` header, and the comment at :166 ("Use fetch instead of Axios — Axios has known multipart issues on Android") makes the bypass deliberate. The refresh machinery lives only on the axios instance (api.ts:83-125). On a non-ok response api.ts:205 throws `new Error(\`Server error ${response.status}: ${errorText}\`)` with no 401 branch (only 429/USAGE_LIMIT is special-cased, :184-202). ResultsScreen.tsx:272-294 catches it: USAGE_LIMIT → Paywall, 503/TIMEOUT → timeout state, everything else → `setLoadError('vision_failed')` at :293, which renders `t('results.emptyState.visionFailed')` (ResultsScreen.tsx:629). By contrast `streamComparison` self-heals: its SSE 401 throws, and the catch falls back to `api.get('/api/v1/text/compare')` (api.ts:509) which does pass through the interceptor.
findings.failure_scenario: The app is backgrounded for longer than the Supabase access-token TTL, the user reopens it and goes straight to camera compare. The identify POST 401s, no refresh is attempted, and the user is told their photos were unreadable ('snap each product in better light') and re-shoots them — every retry fails identically until some other axios call happens to refresh the token.
findings.fix_sketch: On `response.status === 401` inside identifyFromImages, call the same `getOrStartRefresh()` used by the interceptor and retry once with the new token, or route multipart through axios with `transformRequest` left untouched so the interceptor applies.

findings.title: The Arabic logout confirmation carries the account-deletion irreversibility warning
findings.claim: `handleLogout` reuses the delete-account copy and strips the scary clause with `.replace()` on an English literal, which is a no-op in Arabic, so AR users are told logging out cannot be undone.
findings.evidence: ProfileScreen.tsx:304 `Alert.alert(t('profile.logout'), t('profile.deleteConfirm').replace('This cannot be undone.', ''), [...])`. en.json:228 `"profile.deleteConfirm": "Are you sure? This cannot be undone."` → EN renders "Are you sure? ". ar.json:225 `"profile.deleteConfirm": "هل أنت متأكد؟ لا يمكن التراجع عن هذا."` → the English needle is absent, `.replace` returns the string unchanged, and the AR dialog renders "هل أنت متأكد؟ لا يمكن التراجع عن هذا." on a fully reversible action. The catalog-level copy fence (__tests__/copy-policy.test.ts) inspects en.json/ar.json values, not runtime string surgery, so it cannot see this.
findings.failure_scenario: An Arabic user taps Log Out and is warned the action is irreversible. Per Build Principle #4 (CLAUDE.md: 'ZERO scary copy', 'never frame the app as scary') this is a copy-contract violation that lands only in the locale nobody spot-checks, and it plausibly suppresses logouts on shared devices.
findings.fix_sketch: Add a dedicated `profile.logoutConfirm` key to both catalogs and delete the `.replace()`; add a lint/jest rule forbidding `.replace(` on a `t()` result.

findings.title: HistoryScreen's focus effect captures a stale closure and silently discards the active search on every re-focus
findings.claim: `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { loadHistory(); }, []))` freezes the first render's `loadHistory`, which closes over the initial `searchQuery === ''`, so returning to the tab reloads the unfiltered list while the search box still displays the query.
findings.evidence: HistoryScreen.tsx:347-351 `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { loadHistory(); }, []))` — empty dep array, and `loadHistory` is a plain arrow re-created each render (:353) that reads `searchQuery` at :356 `getComparisonHistory(50, 0, searchQuery || undefined)`. `searchQuery` is component state declared at :344 and bound to the TextInput at :775 (`value={searchQuery}`), with the search fired from `onSubmitEditing` at :777-780 calling the *current* `loadHistory`. Nothing resets the input on refocus.
findings.failure_scenario: User types 'iPhone' in History search, submits, gets the filtered list, taps a row to open Results, then goes back. The focus effect runs the frozen `loadHistory` with `searchQuery=''`, so the full 50-row list reappears under a search box that still reads 'iPhone'. The user believes the filter matched everything.
findings.fix_sketch: Hoist `loadHistory` into `useCallback([searchQuery])` and depend on it in the focus effect, or read the query from a ref so the frozen callback still sees the live value.

findings.title: EditProfileScreen's focus effect discards an unsaved display-name edit whenever the user visits the preferences modal
findings.claim: The focus effect unconditionally re-seeds `displayName` from the cached user on every focus, and the screen has an outbound navigation, so returning from it wipes typed input without warning.
findings.evidence: EditProfileScreen.tsx:76-86 — `useFocusEffect(useCallback(() => { (async () => { const u = await getSavedUser(); setUser(u); const n = u?.display_name ?? ''; setDisplayName(n); setInitialName(n); })(); }, []))` with no dirty check. EditProfileScreen.tsx:119 `navigation.navigate('EditPreferences')` is the outbound edge; EditPreferences is a modal that pops back to this screen, re-firing focus. The dirty flag at :88 (`displayName.trim() !== initialName.trim()`) is recomputed from the just-reset values, so the Save button also goes back to disabled — no evidence anything was lost.
findings.failure_scenario: User opens Edit Profile, types a new display name, then taps 'Edit style profile' to adjust priorities first. On returning, the name field has silently reverted to the old value and Save is disabled. The user's edit is gone with no prompt.
findings.fix_sketch: Guard the re-seed on `!dirty`, or seed once on mount and refresh only `user`/`initialName` on focus while leaving `displayName` alone when it differs from `initialName`.

findings.title: Choosing Arabic at onboarding Step 2 hard-reloads the JS bundle and loses all flow state — the documented "orchestrator persists step state" claim is false
findings.claim: `switchLanguage` calls `Updates.reloadAsync()` whenever the RTL direction flips, and OnboardingFlow holds every collected field in un-persisted `useState`, so an Arabic selection at Step 2 restarts the app and the flow from Step 1.
findings.evidence: useLanguage.ts:16-27 — on `I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL` it calls `allowRTL`/`forceRTL` then `require('expo-updates').reloadAsync()`. Step02Language.tsx:26-31 fires it un-awaited (`void switchLanguage(lang); onChange(lang);`) from the language cards, so the reload lands at an unpredictable later tick. OnboardingFlow.tsx:205-206 holds all state in `useState` (`const [step, setStep] = useState(initialStep); const [data, setData] = useState({...})`) and NewOnboardingHost.tsx:85-131 only writes to the backend inside `handleComplete` — there is no AsyncStorage/SecureStore write anywhere in src/screens/onboarding/. The contradicted claim is in featureBucket.ts:19-21 ("The orchestrator (OnboardingFlow) persists step state, so a user who somehow flips buckets mid-onboarding (rare race) still finishes the flow they started") and is repeated in CLAUDE.md's UX-redesign block.
findings.failure_scenario: An Arabic-preferring user on an English-locale device reaches Step 2 and taps العربية. The app reloads (App.tsx remounts, `needsPreferences` is still true) and drops them back at Step 1 of 17 with no explanation. Because the reload is not awaited, a fast tapper can be several steps further along when it fires, losing country/age/priorities selections too.
findings.fix_sketch: Persist `{step, data}` to AsyncStorage on each `setField`/`setStep` and rehydrate via `initialStep`/`initialData` (both props already exist), or defer the RTL reload to the end of onboarding.

findings.title: First launch on an Arabic-locale device renders LTR — forceRTL is applied at boot with no reload
findings.claim: App.tsx calls `I18nManager.forceRTL(true)` during init but never reloads, and RN only applies a direction change on the next app start, so the entire first session shows Arabic text in a left-to-right layout.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:166-173 — `const lang = await getSavedLanguage(); ... const shouldBeRTL = lang === 'ar'; if (I18nManager.isRTL !== shouldBeRTL) { I18nManager.allowRTL(true); I18nManager.forceRTL(shouldBeRTL); }` with no `Updates.reloadAsync()`. The sibling path in useLanguage.ts:20-26 explicitly comments "App restart required for RTL to take effect" and does reload — App.tsx omits it. `getSavedLanguage` (i18n/index.ts:16-17) returns 'ar' from the device locale on a fresh install, before any user choice.
findings.failure_scenario: A user in Bahrain with an Arabic phone installs the app. Session 1: all copy is Arabic but the layout is LTR — the back chevron points the wrong way (`flipForRTL(isRTL)` in OnboardingFlow.tsx:424 reads `I18nManager.isRTL`, still false), slide transitions run backwards (SlideTransition mirrors on `I18nManager.isRTL`), tab bar and list alignment are all mirrored wrong. The whole 17-step onboarding — the first impression — is laid out backwards, and it only corrects on the second cold start.
findings.fix_sketch: After `forceRTL`, call `Updates.reloadAsync()` (guarded for dev) exactly as useLanguage.ts does, before `setIsLoading(false)`.

findings.title: Boot has no failure path — a rejected init or a swallowed font error leaves the app on the splash screen forever
findings.claim: `setIsLoading(false)` is the only exit from the splash gate and it sits after un-try/catch'd awaits; `useAppFonts` discards the loader's error; and the boot path awaits a refresh call on the 120s axios timeout.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:164-206 — inside `init()` the `try` only wraps the auth block (:184-202); `await getSavedLanguage()` (:166), `await import('./src/i18n')` (:167), `await i18n.changeLanguage(lang)` (:168) and `await getStableId()` (:180) are outside it, and `setIsLoading(false)` is the last statement at :203, so any rejection skips it. `init()` is invoked bare at :205 with no `.catch`. App.tsx:245 `if (!fontsLoaded || isLoading || showSplash) return <SplashScreen .../>` is the only gate, and SplashScreen.tsx has no watchdog — its single timer (:33) just calls `onFinish`, which clears `showSplash` but not `isLoading`. theme/fonts.ts:39-45 `const [geistLoaded] = useExpoFonts(...); const [cairoLoaded] = useCairoFonts(...); return geistLoaded && cairoLoaded;` drops both hooks' `error` element, so a font failure is a permanent `false` with no signal. Separately, `initializeAuth()` (:185) awaits `refreshSession()` → `api.post('/api/v1/auth/refresh')` on the shared axios instance whose timeout is 120000ms (api.ts:20) — the health check by contrast passes `{ timeout: 5000 }` (api.ts:262).
findings.failure_scenario: On a captive-portal or high-latency network the boot refresh hangs and the user stares at the splash for up to two minutes before the app becomes usable. If `Localization.getLocales()` (i18n/index.ts:16, outside that function's try) or the font loader fails, the splash is permanent with no error, no retry and no route out — indistinguishable from a hang, and unrecoverable without a reinstall.
findings.fix_sketch: Wrap the whole `init()` body in try/finally with `setIsLoading(false)` in the finally; pass an explicit short timeout to the boot refresh; read and honour the `error` element from both font hooks (render with system fonts rather than blocking).

findings.title: Twelve components (~1,685 LOC) have zero render references, and CLAUDE.md still lists two of them as the design system
findings.claim: Twelve non-test modules are imported by no other non-test module, yet ~17 test files still exercise them and CLAUDE.md advertises two as shipped design-system primitives.
findings.evidence: Cross-referencing every import specifier in non-test src/ + App.tsx against each module leaves twelve with zero inbound references: components/ReferralStatusCard.tsx (298), results/HeroRings.tsx (221), components/ResultsLoadingView.tsx (237), components/StyleProfileCard.tsx (227), components/BonusCountdownCard.tsx (165), primitives/DetailsAccordion.tsx (135), hero/ConcentricMotif.tsx (117), primitives/VsPair.tsx (87), hooks/useTypography.ts (53), primitives/MarqueeCard.tsx (50), components/ComparisonCounter.tsx (48), components/IconButton.tsx (47) — 1,685 LOC. The only surviving mentions are prose comments recording their removal (ProfileScreen.tsx:20-21 "StyleProfileCard (user info moves into ProfileHeaderRow)" / "ReferralStatusCard (not in JSX)"; ResultsScreen.tsx:89 "HeroRings pruned from the render path"). Test files still targeting them include __tests__/components/{BonusCountdownCard,ResultsAccordion.render,HeroRings,HeroRings.sparse}.test.tsx, __tests__/{ReferralStatusCard,ResultsLoadingView,StyleProfileCard*}.test.tsx, __tests__/primitives/{VsPair,MarqueeCard,DetailsAccordion}.test.tsx, __tests__/hooks/useTypography.test.ts. CLAUDE.md's Frontend section states "Components: Button, Card, Chip, SkeletonLoader, ProgressBar, IconButton, ComparisonCounter" — IconButton and ComparisonCounter are both unreachable, so that inventory is wrong.
findings.failure_scenario: Cost is measurable in three places: ~1,685 LOC of unreachable JS in every EAS bundle; ~17 test files whose green status implies coverage of surfaces no user can reach (inflating the coverage number the team steers by); and a design-system inventory in CLAUDE.md that sends the next contributor to two components that do not render.
findings.fix_sketch: Delete the twelve modules with their tests in one commit (git history keeps them for the design-sync references), and correct the CLAUDE.md component list to the primitives actually rendered.

findings.title: lucide-react-native is imported from the barrel at 35 sites for 68 of ~1,500 icons, and Metro does not tree-shake
findings.claim: Every icon import goes through `from 'lucide-react-native'`, whose index re-exports the entire icon set; with the default Expo Metro config (no metro.config.js, no tree shaking) the whole set is emitted into the JS bundle for 68 used icons.
findings.evidence: 35 `import { ... } from 'lucide-react-native'` sites across non-test src/ + App.tsx, resolving to 68 distinct icon names (AlertCircle, ArrowLeft, AtSign, Award … Zap). There is no metro.config.js in SmartCompareApp/ (eslint.config.js:44 lists it as an ignore pattern but the file does not exist), so the project runs Expo's default Metro, which has no cross-module dead-code elimination — `inlineRequires` from babel-preset-expo defers *evaluation* but every re-exported module still ships. The repo already maintains a hand-rolled alternative (src/icons/{ModeIcons,QaranIcon,UtilityIcons}.tsx + index.ts) used elsewhere, so the pattern for avoiding this exists in-tree.
findings.failure_scenario: Roughly 1,430 unused icon components ride in every OTA bundle and every store binary, inflating `eas update` payload size and cold-start parse work on the low-end Android devices that dominate the GCC market — for a feature set that needs 68 glyphs.
findings.fix_sketch: Re-export the 68 used icons from src/icons/index.ts using deep paths (`lucide-react-native/dist/esm/icons/<name>`) and repoint the 35 call sites, or add a babel module-resolver alias; then measure with `npx expo export` before/after.

findings.title: HomeScreen's fallback alert renders the raw backend error string, contradicting the guard the same function documents
findings.claim: The final branch of the stream `onError` handler shows `error.message`, which on the non-streaming fallback path is exactly the backend `error` string that the surrounding comment says must never reach the UI.
findings.evidence: HomeScreen.tsx:381 `Alert.alert(t('common.error'), error.message || t('home.errors.comparison'));` sits directly under the comment at :372-376 ("NEVER the backend error string or scary failure copy. parseApiError returns an empty message for this code precisely so it can never leak into the UI"). That protection covers only `parsed.code === 'TIMEOUT'` (:378-381). The error object reaching the default branch is constructed at api.ts:521-528 as `Object.assign(new Error(response.data.error || 'Comparison failed'), { response: { status: 200, data: { code, error } } })` — so `error.message` *is* `response.data.error` for any non-TIMEOUT structured failure, and is an axios string ('Network Error', 'Request failed with status code 500', 'timeout of 120000ms exceeded') otherwise. Both are untranslated English regardless of locale, and the copy policy bans 'couldn't' / 'try again' / 'Failed to' in user-facing copy (src/i18n/.copy-policy.json scary_vocab_en) — a fence that inspects the catalog only and cannot see a runtime passthrough.
findings.failure_scenario: Backend returns `{success:false, error:"Couldn't finish the comparison — try again.", code:"SOMETHING"}`. parseApiError yields code SOMETHING (not TIMEOUT), the default branch fires, and the banned copy is rendered verbatim in an Alert — in English, to an Arabic user.
findings.fix_sketch: Drop `error.message` from the alert and always render `t('home.errors.comparison')`, adding per-code i18n branches where a distinct message is warranted.

findings.title: HistoryScreen renders parseApiError().message, which is deliberately empty for TIMEOUT/503 — the alert body is blank
findings.claim: `loadHistory`'s non-401 branch alerts with `parseApiError(error).message`, but that helper returns `{ message: '', code: 'TIMEOUT' }` for every 503, producing a titled alert with no body.
findings.evidence: HistoryScreen.tsx:365-367 `if (__DEV__) console.error(...); Alert.alert(t('common.error'), parseApiError(error).message);`. api.ts:635-637 `if (rawCode === 'TIMEOUT' || rawCode === 'STREAM_TIMEOUT' || status === 503) { return { message: '', code: 'TIMEOUT' }; }`, and the contract is stated at api.ts:627-630: "Callers MUST substitute friendly copy by code (results.timeout.*) and IGNORE `message` here". HistoryScreen ignores that contract and never reads `.code`. The same pattern appears at ProfileScreen.tsx:297 `setPasswordError(parseApiError(err).message)`. For non-503 errors the same line leaks the raw backend `error`/`detail` string (api.ts:639-647), which is untranslated.
findings.failure_scenario: Railway restarts or the request 503s while History is loading. The user gets a native alert with the title 'Something went wrong' and a completely empty body and a single OK button — no cause, no retry hint. Every other 5xx shape shows raw English backend text instead.
findings.fix_sketch: Switch on `parseApiError(error).code`: TIMEOUT → `t('results.timeout.body')` with the retry affordance, otherwise `t('history.errors.load')`; never render `.message`.

findings.title: clearSession leaves the previous account's recent searches, usage counter and demographics-prompt state on the device
findings.claim: Logout clears only the two tokens and the cached user, so per-user local state written by four other modules survives into the next account's session on the same device.
findings.evidence: authService.ts:349-357 `clearSession` deletes `qaren_token`, `qaren_refresh_token` (SecureStore) and `@qaren_user` (AsyncStorage) and nothing else. Surviving per-user keys: `@qaren_recent_searches` (HomeScreen.tsx:82, written at :239 with the literal user-typed `"${productA} vs ${productB}"` strings, read unconditionally on every focus at :219-230 via the focus effect at :196-202); `@qaren_free_comparisons_used` (useComparisonCounter.ts:5, :42); the demographics-prompt record in SecureStore (demographicsTrigger.ts:63/:73 — `hasSubmitted`, `dismissedCount`, `lastDismissedAt`), whose only reset is `demographicsTrigger.ts:111` in a separate exported helper that `clearSession` never calls.
findings.failure_scenario: Two people share a phone (common in the target market) or one user signs out and another signs in. The second user's Home screen shows the first user's recent product searches verbatim as tappable chips, and inherits their demographics-prompt suppression state so the cohort prompt never appears for them.
findings.fix_sketch: Have `clearSession` also remove `@qaren_recent_searches` and `@qaren_free_comparisons_used` and call `demographicsTrigger`'s existing reset (:111); add a regression test asserting the full key set is cleared.

findings.title: Hardcoded English strings survive in rendered UI because the eslint i18n fence is jsx-text-only and never runs
findings.claim: Six user-visible English literals sit in screens and components that the i18next lint rule either cannot see (props, template literals) or would flag but is never executed against.
findings.evidence: The winner badge alone is rendered three incompatible ways and only the dead one is translated: LoadingScreenVariants.tsx:408 hardcodes `<Text style={streamingStyles.badgeText}>Top match</Text>`; TopMatchBadge.tsx:31 calls `t('results.topMatch', { defaultValue: 'Top match' })` for a key that exists in neither catalog (it is one of the 65 in frontend-04); and the key that does exist and IS translated — en.json:120 / ar.json:117 `"results.bestPick": "Top match" / "الأفضل"` — is referenced by zero call sites. So both live render paths emit English to Arabic users. (Separately, the orphan's AR value "الأفضل" is the superlative form the EN policy bans as `Best Pick`/`Best Choice` while `banned_ar` omits the bare word, so reviving that key would need a copy review first.) Also: PaywallScreen.tsx:331/339/347 `<Text ...>Today</Text>` / `In 2 days` / `In 3 days`, inlined next to translated `t('paywall.timeline.*')` calls. Outside the rule's `jsx-text-only` mode: ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:70 `return \`${hrs}h\`` and :73 `return \`${days}d\`` — English suffixes inside a function whose other two branches correctly use `t('profile.recent.justNow')` and `t('profile.recent.yesterday')`; ResultsContent.tsx:194 `accessibilityLabel="Back"` and :208 `accessibilityLabel="Share"`; EditPreferencesFlow.tsx:129 `t('common.close')` where `common.close` exists in neither catalog and no `defaultValue` is supplied, so i18next returns the key and VoiceOver announces the literal string "common.close". eslint.config.js:52-63 configures `i18next/no-literal-string` as `'error'` over src/screens + src/components, but per frontend-05 eslint is not in CI and package.json's `lint` script is never invoked.
findings.failure_scenario: An Arabic user watching a comparison stream sees an English 'Top match' badge on the winning card; the Paywall's trial timeline reads 'In 2 days · تذكير لطيف قبل الفوترة'; Profile's recent decisions read '5h' and '3d'; and the Results back/share buttons plus the preferences close button are announced in English (or as a raw i18n key) by an Arabic screen reader.
findings.fix_sketch: Replace each literal with the existing or a new key (`results.bestPick` already covers the badge), add `common.close` to both catalogs, and run eslint in CI so the fence stops being decorative.

findings.title: Arabic dates render in the Hijri calendar and prices use device-locale digits inconsistently
findings.claim: `formatDate` hardcodes the `ar-SA` locale, whose CLDR default calendar is islamic-umalqura, and price formatting calls `toLocaleString()` with no locale while two other components pass 'en-US' explicitly.
findings.evidence: formatDate.ts:14-15 `const locale = language === 'ar' ? 'ar-SA' : 'en-US'; return date.toLocaleDateString(locale, { month: 'short', day: 'numeric' });` — `ar-SA` resolves to the Umm al-Qura calendar under full ICU, so the returned month/day is Hijri, not Gregorian. `formatTimeAgo` falls through to it for anything older than 7 days (formatDate.ts:33) and is consumed by HistoryScreen.tsx:46/:395 — the same screen whose section headers ('Today' / 'Yesterday' / 'This week' / 'Older', HistoryScreen.tsx:386-390) are computed from Gregorian millisecond diffs. Locale-free number formatting: ResultsContent.tsx:129 and ResultsScreen.tsx:396 `\`${price.currency} ${price.amount.toLocaleString()}\``, plus ResultsAccordion.tsx:221/:661 — device locale, so Arabic-locale devices can render Arabic-Indic digits; hero/LoadingRings.tsx:58 and primitives/StatBlock.tsx:29 pass 'en-US' explicitly, and ProfileEditorialSections.tsx:74 passes nothing.
findings.failure_scenario: An Arabic user's history shows a comparison from 10 days ago labelled with a Hijri date (e.g. '٧ رمضان') sitting under a section header derived from the Gregorian calendar, and the same session renders '٢٥٫٩٩' on the Results price line while the loading counter above it renders '25.99' — two digit systems for the same number, one screen apart.
findings.fix_sketch: Use `'ar'` (or `'ar-BH-u-ca-gregory'`) in formatDate.ts:14, and give every `toLocaleString` call the same explicit locale + `{ minimumFractionDigits: 2 }` via one shared money formatter.

findings.title: The mount-only-fetch staleness class covers the savings banner and trending list too, not just SmartPickCard
findings.claim: All three Home editorial sections and the usage counter fetch inside `useEffect(..., [])` on a tab screen that never unmounts, so a comparison completed this session leaves stale figures on Home for its whole duration.
findings.evidence: HomeEditorialSections.tsx:55-71 (SmartPickCard, `getHomeSmartPick`), :268-284 (SavingsBanner, `getHomeSavings`), :317-330 (TrendingCard, `getHomeTrending`) — all three are `useEffect(..., [])`. useComparisonCounter.ts:16-35 is the same shape for `getUsageStatus`. HomeScreen itself uses `useFocusEffect` for its other loads (HomeScreen.tsx:129-153, :196-202), so the pattern is understood but not applied to these children. CLAUDE.md's Cache-bust section names only "SmartPickCard same-session staleness remains as Bundle F item" — that status is still accurate, but the savings banner and trending list are the same defect and are not recorded anywhere.
findings.failure_scenario: User runs a comparison that saves BHD 12, returns to Home, and the 'This month · X BHD shopped smarter · Across N decisions sorted with Qaren' banner still shows the pre-comparison figures — a numerically wrong claim about the user's own money — until the app is cold-started. The free-comparisons pill has the same problem, worsened by camera compares never calling `increment()` (only HomeScreen.tsx:328 and :416, the text and url paths, do).
findings.fix_sketch: Swap the three `useEffect([])` calls and the counter hydrate to `useFocusEffect(useCallback(...))`, matching HomeScreen.tsx:196; and call `increment()` on the camera completion path.

findings.title: Certificate pinning initialisation is fired without await, so the boot request can race the pin
findings.claim: `setupCertificatePinning()` is an async function invoked bare at api.ts module scope and `pinningInitialized` only flips after the native call resolves, so any request issued before that resolution is unpinned.
findings.evidence: api.ts:16 `setupCertificatePinning();` — no `await`, no promise retained, and no request-side gate. certificatePinning.ts:35-51 `export async function setupCertificatePinning(): Promise<void> { if (pinningInitialized) return; try { await initializeSslPinning({...}); pinningInitialized = true; }` — the flag is set only after the native bridge call completes. Nothing in api.ts's request interceptor (:24-38) or in the raw-`fetch` call sites (api.ts:167, :410; authService.ts:495, :608) waits on it. App.tsx's boot path reaches `initializeAuth()` → `refreshSession()` → `api.post('/api/v1/auth/refresh')` (authService.ts:221) on the same tick sequence as module init.
findings.failure_scenario: On a cold start the token-refresh POST — carrying the refresh token — can leave the device before the SPKI pin set is installed, so it is protected by system trust only. On a device with an attacker-installed user CA (or a corporate MITM proxy) that single request is interceptable even though the app ships pinning specifically to prevent it.
findings.fix_sketch: Keep the promise (`const pinningReady = setupCertificatePinning();`) and `await pinningReady` at the top of the axios request interceptor and before each raw `fetch`, so no request can precede the pin.

findings.title: Sentry initialises unconditionally, so development crashes and 10% traces are billed to the production project
findings.claim: `Sentry.init` is called from App.tsx module scope with no `__DEV__` or `enabled` gate, so every local dev session reports to the same `qaren-rr/react-native` DSN as production.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:9-10 `import { initSentry } from './src/services/sentry'; initSentry();` at module top. sentry.ts:132-141 `Sentry.init({ dsn: resolved, sendDefaultPii: false, tracesSampleRate: 0.1, beforeSend: scrubBeforeSend })` — no `enabled`, `environment`, or `enableInExpoDevelopment` field, and the DSN falls back to the hardcoded FALLBACK_DSN at sentry.ts:57-58 whenever `EXPO_PUBLIC_SENTRY_DSN` is unset (which it is in every local run).
findings.failure_scenario: Every reload-time error, every intentional crash test and 10% of dev navigation transactions consume production Sentry quota and pollute the issue list that release triage depends on, making 'is this real user impact?' unanswerable without manual filtering.
findings.fix_sketch: Pass `enabled: !__DEV__` (or set `environment: __DEV__ ? 'development' : 'production'` and filter server-side) in the `Sentry.init` options.

findings.title: CLAUDE.md documents @sentry/react-native@8.11.1; package.json pins ~7.2.0
findings.claim: The documented Sentry SDK major version does not match the one the project actually resolves, so any version-specific guidance derived from the doc is wrong.
findings.evidence: package.json:19 `"@sentry/react-native": "~7.2.0"`. CLAUDE.md's Frontend → Services block states: "`sentry.ts` — `@sentry/react-native@8.11.1`. Mirrors backend `before_send` scrub …". A full major version apart.
findings.failure_scenario: A contributor reading CLAUDE.md applies v8 API guidance (v8 changed the `beforeSend`/integration surface) to a v7 install, or assumes an upgrade already landed when planning the sourcemap-upload follow-up that sentry.ts:16-19 defers.
findings.fix_sketch: Correct the CLAUDE.md line to `~7.2.0`, or land the v8 upgrade and re-verify `scrubBeforeSend` against the v8 event shape.

findings.title: react-native-markdown-display is eagerly bundled for two rarely-opened modal screens
findings.claim: The markdown renderer and its markdown-it dependency chain are imported at module scope by a screen registered in the root navigator, so they load for every user even though only Privacy and Terms use them.
findings.evidence: LegalScreen.tsx:18 `import Markdown from 'react-native-markdown-display';`, used once at :107 `<Markdown style={markdownStyles}>{content}</Markdown>`. It is the only consumer of the package in the whole app (one import site across all of src/). App.tsx:47 imports LegalScreen statically and registers it at :319-323 as a `Stack.Screen`, so the module graph is resolved at bundle time regardless of whether the route is ever visited. LegalScreen is reachable only from Profile → Privacy/Terms and PaywallScreen.tsx:384-388.
findings.failure_scenario: markdown-it plus the renderer's component tree ship in every EAS update and store binary for a screen the median user never opens — pure payload cost on the same low-bandwidth OTA path as frontend-16.
findings.fix_sketch: Lazy-load it inside LegalScreen (`const Markdown = React.lazy(...)` or a dynamic `require()` inside the render branch that has content), the same technique ResultsScreen.tsx:189/:237 already uses for api.ts helpers.

findings.title: Deep links to Register with an invite code silently fail once the user is authenticated
findings.claim: The linking config routes `r/:code` and `redeem?code=` through the `Auth` screen, which is only registered in the unauthenticated branch of the navigator, so those links resolve to nothing for a signed-in user.
findings.evidence: App.tsx:256-269 declares `Auth: { screens: { Register: { path: 'r/:code', parse: {...} } } }`, and App.tsx:270-282's `getStateFromPath` rewrite funnels `redeem?code=…` into the same `r/<code>` pattern. But `Stack.Screen name="Auth"` is rendered only under `{!isAuthenticated ? (...)` (App.tsx:289-294); when authenticated the navigator renders the Main/Results/Legal/... branch with no `Auth` route. By contrast ReferralLanding and InviteeQuiz were deliberately hoisted out of both branches (App.tsx:396-411) precisely so their deep links always resolve — `r/:code` did not get the same treatment.
findings.failure_scenario: An existing signed-in user taps a friend's `https://qaren.app/r/QR-ABC123` share link. React Navigation cannot resolve `Auth.Register`, so the app opens on Home with the invite dropped — no error, no fallback, and the referral attribution for that link is lost.
findings.fix_sketch: Either route the code to a screen that exists in both branches (ReferralLanding already is) or handle the authenticated case explicitly — read the code and surface a 'you're already signed in' path rather than resolving to nothing.
